title: Consolidated eval-driven acceptance and launch checklist for unified generation & retrieval endpoints
creator: Ava Chen
description: Purpose: Produce a single PRD-grade acceptance and launch playbook that verifies behavioral fidelity, latency/cost SLOs, and operational readiness for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints. Focus is on evaluation-driven acceptance using curated prompt sets, automated quality gating, canary thresholds and rollout heuristics. This ticket collects requirements, defines pass/fail criteria, and lists the launch checklist items required for go/no-go. Non-goal: this ticket does not implement model-level tuning or replace model onboarding flow; it defines the acceptance gates for the hosted API surface only.
scope: Include: chat (chat-completions semantics), completions (stateless prompt->text), embeddings, rerank (scoring/rerank API). Deliverables: PRD acceptance criteria, curated prompt/benchmark sets, automated smoke-tests and CI job, canary rollout thresholds, operator runbook and rollback steps, dashboard panels. Exclude: private/Dedicated-specific infra changes, billing contract adjustments, OSS SDK changes (those are separate tickets).
non_goals: 1) No model retraining or dataset creation. 2) No changes to customer-facing SDK semantics. 3) No on-prem deployment packaging in this ticket.
requirements: Behavioral acceptance harness: shareable prompt sets covering 500+ edge cases per surface (generation hallucination checks, instruction-following, safety prompts, paraphrase resilience).

Quality metrics: define pass threshold for semantic similarity (embeddings), top-1 rerank NDCG@10 baseline, generation exact match + acceptability ratios. Each threshold must be tied to a baseline model version.
Performance SLOs: p95 latency targets per endpoint for default config (chat: 200ms token latency, completions: 120ms token latency, embeddings: 50ms per vector, rerank: 150ms per request).
Cost guardrails: median token unit cost must be within 15% of current production profile for model families on the hosted lane.
Telemetry: structured event schema for request/response, prompt fingerprint, model-family tag, KV-cache hit metric, batching size distribution.
Operational: alert thresholds for error-rate, tail-latency, model-degraded-quality regressions (as measured by eval harness).
Rollout policy: scripted canary with 3-stage rollout (internal <5%, partner beta 5-20%, global >=60%) with automatic pause on metric breach.
Backfill: migration notes and SDK compatibility checks for customers using legacy endpoints; deprecation windows documented.
acceptance_criteria: PRD acceptance harness committed to repo: /repos/internal/pm/acceptance-harness with readme and usage instructions.
Quality: For each endpoint run the curated prompt set and meet thresholds vs baseline model (see links). Failure modes documented and triaged before go/no-go.
SLOs: p50/p95 latency tests executed across regions and recorded in dashboard. No more than 1 region may exceed p95 target by 20% during canary for go decision.
Reliability: system error-rate <0.5% for successful canary traffic over 24 hours. Any burst errors automatically rollback policy triggers.
Regression alarms: automated daily eval comparing new model/version to baseline; if quality delta >5% for critical prompts, block rollout.
Security & compliance: security review completed and KMS integration validated for request logs; audit log test vectors executed.
Observability: dashboard panels (cost/latency/error/quality) visible in Console and linked in playbook; alert runbook steps present.
Operator runbook: manual rollback steps + reheating cache instructions + escalation contacts present and validated in a tabletop run.
per_endpoint_acceptance: Chat: sample-conversations suite (1200 cases) executed; expected instruction-following rate >= 95% and hallucination flag rate <= baseline + 2%. Must pass streaming sanity tests (chunk continuity, token ordering).
Completions: completion-length distribution checks and stop-sequence reliability tests. Determinism sampling smoke (seeded runs) must remain within acceptable variance.
Embeddings: embedding cosine baseline stability test (anchor-centroid variance < 0.02) and retrieval recall sweep using 10k test items; average recall@100 must not drop more than 3% vs baseline.
Rerank: NDCG@10 measured on standard query set (2k queries) and synthetic adversarial queries; must exceed baseline by tolerance or show no more than 2% degradation on critical queries.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Internal canary (incubate) - 1% internal traffic for 24h: smoke tests and ops drills. Metrics tracked in real-time dashboard.
Stage 1: Partner beta - 5-20% traffic with selected partners for 72h, include end-to-end billing and contract checks.
Stage 2: Regional ramp - sequentially open regions (US-East -> US-West -> EU) with 6h observation windows between steps.
Stage 3: Global ramp with automated progressive traffic increase up to 100% over 48h with final stability window of 7 days.

Auto-pause: if any of the following triggers occur during ramp - error-rate spike >1% delta, p95 latency >200% of target, quality regression >5% on critical prompts - then pause and rollback to previous stable variant.
launch_checklist: Acceptance harness PR merged and CI green (link to PR).
Dashboards created and validated in Console (links provided).
Security review ticket closed (link to security ticket).
Billing test completed with partner account and sandbox data.
Operator runbook published and tabletop executed (list of participants).
SDK compatibility smoke (JavaScript/Python) executed and docs updated with migration notes.
Canary automation pipeline configured (GitHub Actions / internal CD job).
Customer-facing release notes drafted and signoff from comms.

risks_mitigations: Risk: latent quality regressions visible only at scale. Mitigation: extended partner beta and automated daily evals with alerting.
Risk: cost-per-token spike after batching changes. Mitigation: simulated cost projection runs and throttled rollout with cost guardrails in CD.
Risk: observed tail-latency regressions in specific regions. Mitigation: regional rollback knobs and routing fallback to previously stable model family.
